title: Phase B3 slice 1 (D-076): proposal-check route - check_proposal endpoint carrying BP-1..BP-7, T053-wave residual closures, and the G4 fold-in tests
objective: Wire the accepted B2 proposal-check engine to its first (internal, flag-gated) HTTP seam: a proposal-checks endpoint that accepts a proposed_massing payload + lot context, runs the B0 validation and the B2 check_proposal engine, and returns the grouped PASS/FAIL/COULD-NOT-CHECK results with numeric shortfalls for the editor UI (B3 slice 2) to consume. The route is the trust boundary: all seven G5-recorded preconditions BP-1..BP-7 are enforced here. Also close the four T053-wave route residuals (400-cap truncation branch, 500-path, surrogate strict-JSON guard half, shared-flag coupling note) and bind the four G4-advisory branches of the B2 module with tests (AMBIGUOUS_RULE, NO_APPLICABLE_RULE, commensurable MINIMUM direction, street-line finiteness + LotContext type guard).
business_reason: B2 gave us the check engine; this route is the ONE trust boundary between editor input and that engine - it carries every security precondition the G5 wave recorded, and it is the seam the editor UI (B3 slice 2) will call
inputs: CHECKPOINT ENVELOPE (binding): in every checkpoint, OMIT the four envelope fields (branch, worktree, starting_sha, current_sha) entirely - the controller fills the authoritative values. If you supply one it must be EXACT full-length (40-hex SHA, FULL worktree path).

REPORT DISCIPLINE (binding): reference files and line anchors, never embed long verbatim sections; every checkpoint carries IMPLEMENTATION; one concise evidence pass. The review-round budget is spent on code, not reports.
COMMAND CWD (binding): run ruff + api pytest from services/api (`cd services/api` first; cwd persists; `cd ../..` before the modularity check from repo root). Never chain onto a documented command.

CODE-GRAPH NAVIGATION BLOCK (D-066-R001; graph current at this contract seam). The accepted seams you CONSUME READ-ONLY: app/rules/proposal_checks.py (B2 engine - check_proposal is the ONLY entry you may call, never derive_proposal directly: BP-1), app/scenario/proposal_input_gate.py (T053's DB-034(a)/(b) input gate - reuse it; if it is insufficient for this route, surface a discovery, never edit it), app/scenario/proposal.py (validator), app/scenario/derivation.py (LotContext types). api/v1/proposal_validation.py (T053's route; consumed by main.py + its test file) is IN scope ONLY for the four residual closures. main.py mounts routers (T053 precedent at its condo/validation mounts). Run `python tools/code_graph/query.py --no-regen impact <path>` before any sweep; the graph is ADVISORY - verify in source.

SCOPE 1/3 - THE CHECK ROUTE (binding; read docs/PROPOSAL_EDITOR_PHASED_PLAN.md phase-B B3 row, project-control/reports/M5-T054-G5.md (BP-1..BP-7 verbatim), M5-T054-G4.md (G4-1..G4-4), docs/DISCOVERY_BACKLOG.md rows DB-034/DB-035/DB-036, and api/v1/proposal_validation.py FIRST): NEW route module services/api/app/api/v1/proposal_checks_api.py mounted in main.py - internal, flag-gated on the EXISTING INTERNAL_RULE_EVAL_ENABLED (flag off = the same not-found behavior as T053's route; include_in_schema=False; no new flag, no new public surface). POST payload: the proposed_massing block + lot context (area, provenance, lot-line segments, optional attested street lines) + lot rule facts + scenario_label/proposal_id. Behavior: (1) request boundary FIRST - reuse the T053 input-gate discipline for size/strings (read-only reuse); enforce BP-2 (scenario_label + proposal_id: explicit length caps and a conservative charset, typed refusal) and BP-7 (bounded request body; this is an internal route - no auth change in this packet, record the disposition that authn/tenancy arrive with the public exposure packet); (2) BP-4 compute budget - enforce ROUTE-LEVEL practical caps TIGHTER than the library ceilings (exterior walls and lot-line segments capped so the documented worst-case wall-by-segment product stays under ~1e6 segment tests; show the arithmetic in a comment + test), typed refusal naming the cap; (3) BP-5 - validate lot_rule_facts VALUE types/domains against the evaluator's input vocabulary before feeding (bad type/domain = typed 422 naming the exact field; unmapped keys are surfaced in the response as unmapped, never fed); (4) call check_proposal ONCE (BP-1) and serialize the grouped report (results with provided/required/unit/shortfall, could_not_check reasons, summary counts incl. could_not_check_count) for the editor; (5) BP-3 - EVERY error path length-caps embedded values: wrap the call so a propagated ProposalDerivationError/ProposedMassingError detail is length-capped before serialization (the B0 validator's uncapped vertex repr class from G5-3 must never reach a response uncapped); (6) BP-6/DB-034(d) - this route emits NO scenario document and NO contract version; prove it and record the disposition (emission stays with the scenario-workspace save path, B3 slice 2 territory).

SCOPE 2/3 - T053 ROUTE RESIDUALS (binding): in api/v1/proposal_validation.py + tests/api/test_proposal_validation_api.py close the four recorded residuals: (a) the 400-cap truncation branch gets a binding test (an over-cap payload whose refusal detail is truncated to the exact cap); (b) the 500-path gets a test (a forced internal error returns the typed bounded 500, no stack/value leak); (c) the surrogate half of the strict-JSON guard gets a test (a lone-surrogate payload refuses typed); (d) the shared-flag coupling note: add the explicit test that BOTH routes (validation + checks) gate on the same flag and their off-behavior is identical (the coupling is deliberate; the test documents it).

SCOPE 3/3 - G4 FOLD-IN TESTS (binding): in services/api/tests/rules/test_proposal_checks.py add the four binding tests the G4 wave recorded (M5-T054-G4.md): (1) AMBIGUOUS_RULE - two usable same-family rules yield could_not_check/ambiguous_rule with required_value None (never picks a winner); (2) NO_APPLICABLE_RULE - an applicable-elsewhere rule with non-matching facts yields could_not_check/no_applicable_rule; (3) a commensurable MINIMUM-direction check exercising _compare's minimum branch end-to-end (PASS when provided>=required; FAIL with shortfall = required-provided); (4) street-line coordinate finiteness + the lot-must-be-LotContext guard refusals. Use the existing fixture registry pattern; hand-computed values with shown arithmetic; NO edit to app/rules/proposal_checks.py itself (its behavior is accepted - these tests BIND existing behavior).

PRESERVATION (binding): app/rules/**, app/scenario/** (incl. proposal_input_gate.py), packages/contracts/**, apps/web/** are READ-ONLY; proposal_validation.py changes are LIMITED to the residual closures (accepted semantics byte-preserved otherwise); main.py change is the one mount line (T053 precedent); every existing suite green unchanged; no new dependency; no new flag; modularity: the route module focused and below warn tier.
Discovery routing (D-069): surface out-of-scope findings in the report; never fix in-packet. No WebFetch. Thin client. Run `python -m ruff check .` from services/api before every checkpoint.
